TITLE: Apple Q4 2026: price beats, memory caps the margin
QUOTE: What we’re seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented. … For the December quarter, we expect even higher memory costs, partly offset by a few factors.
QUOTE_WHO: John Ternus, CEO, fiscal Q4 2026 earnings call, 2 November 2026
COMPANY_INTRO: Apple sells the iPhone, about half of revenue, plus Mac, iPad, wearables and services such as the App Store, across over 2.5bn active devices. Fiscal 2026 revenue USD 479bn; Nasdaq-listed, worth about USD 5tn.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Beat
TAKEAWAYS.text: Revenue USD 114.5bn (+1% vs. consensus) and EPS USD 2.10 (+5.5%), led by iPhone and Mac pricing.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Reaction
TAKEAWAYS.text: Shares down over 4% pre-market on 3 November: a 45% to 46% margin guide undercut the beat.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Watch
TAKEAWAYS.text: Services growth guided to 8% to 9%, from 10%, as licensing and App Store changes bite.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Valuation
TAKEAWAYS.text: 35.2x forward earnings, near the highest since 2010: little room for further margin slippage.

H_P1: Record iPhone cycle, costs outrunning price
P1_PARAGRAPH: Revenue beat consensus by 1% and EPS by 5.5%, yet the shares fell 3.5% after hours and more than 4% pre-market on 3 November. The beat leaned on price rises; the December-quarter margin guide of 45% to 46% is 80bp below consensus. Apple is short of supply, not demand. The question is how much memory inflation pricing can absorb.
C1_TITLE: AAPL: Q4 2026 results and December-quarter guide vs. consensus
C1_SUB: Surprise vs. LSEG consensus of 2 November 2026 · sales and EPS in %, margins and growth guide in points · *ex tariff refunds · guides at midpoint
C1_COMMENT: Hardware carried the quarter: Mac beat by 12% and iPhone by 2%, both supply-constrained after price increases. iPad and wearables missed by 7% and 8% on tough comparisons. Ex tariff refunds, EPS beat by 3% and gross margin fell about 60bp short. The guide splits the same way: sales above consensus, margin below.
BASE_CASE: Apple’s hardware cycle is its strongest since fiscal 2021, with revenue up 15% and EPS up 20% to USD 8.98, but its pricing power now pays for memory rather than lifting margin. Demand has held through the price rises. Consensus forward EPS of USD 9.58 implies only 7% growth, which we see as achievable with gross margin at 45% to 46%. At 35.2x, that delivery is priced and the risk/reward is balanced. iPhone Duo supply is the catalyst; the next test is the December-quarter margin in early 2027.
UPSIDE: December-quarter gross margin at or above 46%; iPhone Duo supply in balance with demand by spring 2027; Services back to 10% growth as Siri AI lifts paid subscriptions and iCloud+.
DOWNSIDE: A March-quarter margin guide below 45%; unit declines once the September iPhone price rise works through; further App Store rulings taking Services growth below 8%.
H_A1: Results: price and the Mac did the work
A1_PARAGRAPHS: Revenue rose 12% to USD 114.5bn, above the 9% to 11% guide, despite nearly 2 points of sequential currency headwind. iPhone grew 17% to USD 57.6bn, a September-quarter record, with record upgraders in the US, mainland China and India; Mac grew 24% to USD 10.8bn on MacBook Neo and MacBook Pro. Both were supply-constrained, mainly by advanced-node chip availability. iPad fell 10% and wearables 8% against launches a year ago. Services rose 10% to USD 31.6bn, in line, with paid subscriptions above 1.5bn. Operating expenses rose 21% on research spending, so operating income grew 10%, and buybacks lifted EPS growth to 14%.

The beat and the share price fall, 3.5% after hours on 2 November and more than 4% pre-market on 3 November, diverge, and the confirmed drivers sit in the margin line. Ex the 1-point tariff refund, gross margin was about 46.9%, 60bp below consensus, and EPS beat by 3% rather than 5.5%. Management guided the December-quarter margin to 45% to 46% against 46.3% expected, said memory prices keep rising beyond December and disclosed USD 33bn more purchase obligations since June. We think positioning added to the move: the shares had risen 25% in twelve months against 16% for forward earnings.
A2_PARAGRAPH: Apple guides December-quarter revenue up 7% to 10%, on top of 16% growth a year ago and against 6.1% expected: the midpoint implies about USD 156bn, which management expects to be the best quarter in its history. The guide reflects constrained supply: iPhone Duo is short of demand, and Mac and iPad are now limited by memory. Services should grow 8% to 9%, slowed by third-party licensing, App Store changes and currency. Gross margin of 45% to 46% compares with 48.2% a year ago, with most of the decline from memory plus Siri AI ramp costs. Management says it is too early to read price elasticity.
H_C2: Valuation: a peak multiple on slower growth
C2_TITLE: AAPL: share price vs. consensus earnings and valuation
C2_SUB: Weekly, January 2010 to 2 November 2026 · Bloomberg BEst 12m-forward EPS · 40-week simple MA · log scale · P/E vs. its 2010 to 2026 average · last price: 2 November close, pre-release
C2_COMMENT: The shares have run ahead of earnings: up 25% over twelve months against 16% for consensus forward EPS. The 12-month forward P/E of 35.2x is 83% above its 19.3x average since 2010, close to the 36.1x peak of 23 October and above the one-year average of 32.1x. The price sits 13% above its 40-week average of USD 301. Consensus EPS slipped 0.4% to USD 9.58 on 3 November; a further 5% cut at an unchanged price would take the multiple to 37x. A return to the one-year average needs a 10% upgrade, which the margin guide does not support.
SOURCE_LINE: Source: Syz Research, Bloomberg, LSEG consensus, company filings, Apple fiscal Q4 2026 results release and earnings call of 2 November 2026, analyst research notes of 3 November 2026
